# Semibold and already-bold ink controls

Original OOXML generated by `tools/semibold_ink_fixture.py`, using our existing
minimal package boilerplate. Eighteen paragraphs cover Franklin Gothic Demi,
Arial Black and Arial Bold, at 8/12/24 pt with w:b off/on. These are installed
Windows fonts; no font binaries or corpus content are bundled with the source.
The reference application exported the retained one-page PDF. The JSON pins source/PDF
hashes and records 384-dpi ink sums with baseline-relative crop boxes.

Current result: with local-font permission granted, all eighteen regular/bold
samples pass the unchanged 5% native ink bound. The generic metadata-assisted
synthesis probe recognizes Demi as a non-bold face without a font-name
exception. The suite exercises both granted and ungranted permission states.
Without permission, Demi bold still has only 81-82% of the native ink; that
scenario retains an explicit expected failure after validating regular ink.
Arial Black and Arial Bold pass in both states. Missing reference fonts are
explicitly skipped, and source/reference hashes remain checked.
Despite its name, the installed FRADM.TTF reports OS/2 weight 400,
fsSelection 64 and head.macStyle 0. Arial Black reports weight 900 and Arial
Bold reports 700. Treat these as measured facts; do not assume a numeric
semibold weight from the font name. Both local full-name and PostScript-name
aliases currently have identical regular/bold browser ink for the Demi face.

Regenerate the DOCX, export it with `tools/export-reference.ps1`, then use
`tools/record_synthetic_bold_ink.py control.docx native.pdf reference.json
--reference-version 16.0.20326` with full paths. The measurement tool also serves the
existing synthetic-bold controls. Relevant bold property: ECMA-376 §17.3.2.1.
